title: Graceland
annotation:
Recorded in three different places:

    * Vusi Khumalo, Makhaya Mahlangu, Bakithi Kumalo, Chikapa “Ray” Phiri, and Demola Adepoju were recorded by Peter Thwaites at Ovation Studios, Johannesburg, South Africa
    * Paul Simon and The Everly Brothers were recorded by Steven Strassman at Amigo Studios, Los Angeles, USA and by Mark Cobrin at The Hits Factory, New York, NY, USA

annotation: This version of Helen Reddy’s iconic hit single and feminist anthem was recorded at Sun West Studio on Hollywood Boulevard in Los Angeles. It is the most famous version of the song, with [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Am_Woman#The_recording_session|some of the best session musicians] of the day assembled. The recording builds nicely with the addition of a brass backing from the second chorus and strong back-up vocals.

annotation:
There is no true stereo mix of She Loves You as the original master was lost.

The following releases use a mock stereo remaster of this mix for stereo:
US: Capitol ST 2080 Second 1964.
Germany: Odeon SMO 83 991 (later 1C 062-04 207) Beatles Greatest 1965, Odeon STO 73 692 (later 1C 062-04 363) Beatles Beat 1966.

1964 Capitol mono remaster used:
US: Capitol T 2080 Second 1964.

Geoff Emerick entered room 53 at Abbey Road on November 8, 1966, and spent an hour and a half (4 to 5:30 pm) constructing two mixes of the song. The first one was made by cutting all the high frequencies from the left channel and cutting all the low frequencies from the right channel. This is the one that made it onto A Collection of Oldies, Parlophone PCS 7016, which was released in Britain only on December 9, 1966. The second mix had Emerick shift the track from channel to channel during different portions of the song, which wasn't used. The following releases use this remaster:
UK: Parlophone PCS 7016 Collection of Oldies 1966, Apple PCSP 717 The Beatles 1962-1966 1973.

The following mock stereo remaster was created by Capitol in 1973:
US: Apple SKBO-3403 The Beatles 1962-1966 1973.

The sonic restoration by Peter Mew for the 1992 mono remaster, made originally for the EP set in 1992, sounds much better than the original master. The following releases use the 1992 remaster:
CD: EMI C2 15852 (EP box set) 1992, EMI CDP 7 97036 2 The Beatles 1962-1966 1993.

title: Waves
disambiguation: "1999" Version, Sample at 2:10 starts with "What the rap audience ain't ready for..."
annotation:
The song has an intro / verse 1 / interlude sample / verse 2 structure. 2 versions of this song came out, with the difference being the intro sample, and the spoken recording used in the interlude. The interlude for this version is:

"What the rap audience ain't ready for is a real person. You know what I want to say, a real N-I-G-G-A. I'm coming at 'em 100% real, I ain't compromising anything. Anything that talk about me got a problem, you know what I'm saying? It's going to be straight up, like if I was a street person. That's how I'm coming at the whole world. And I'm doing real about it, and I'ma grow with my music."

It is a [artist:98b5a1d4-3f58-412f-950c-ee9d82743705|Tupac] sample from a [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tHOrL-qcwRU&t=71s|1997 MTV Special called "Tupac Shakur in his Own Words"]
